title: Klink Cycles Opens Preorder For Trash Panda ATTB Framesets
content:
Many bikes handle well off-road; other bikes carry things well. Few can do both. The Trash Panda is inspired by cycle-truck style cargo bikes; by attaching the load to the frame instead of the steering, the bike maintains nimble handling while carrying serious cargo. Cycle-trucks use a 20” front wheel, leaving room for large cargo to stay out of the handlebars’ way. This type of rack, if mounted on a 29” wheel, leaves little room before the cargo prevents the bars from turning. A 26” wheel is the ideal compromise, providing sufficient rollover and efficiency for rugged terrain, while still allowing for a cycle-truck style cargo rack.

Though it’s rated for up to 40lbs on the front rack, it’s not a cargo bike. Though it clears up to a 2.6” knobby tire, it’s not a mountain bike. Nor is it a shreddy city commuter. Sure, if you try hard enough, you can do most things on most any bike. But if you’re looking for an ATTB and something to haul your kids to school, a trail rig, or an urban runabout, you might actually need two more bikes ;)

The rear-end geometry was developed by framebuilder Leo Cruces, inspired by years of bike touring on the rugged forest roads of the Oregon Cascades, with special influence from studying the Soma tradesman, Jones LWB, various Rivendells, and the very first mountain bikes from the repack era Marin County.

Klink Cycles Trash Panda ATTB Quick Hits

  • Limited to 15 frames
  • $950 Deposit for $2500 frameset
  • Delivery in April of 2027
  • Oﬀ-Road Front-Load Optimized Geometry
  • Frame-Mounted Cargo Rack
  • Mixed wheel size: 26” Front and 29” Rear
  • Ultra wide-range gearing (it’s front-derailleur-friendly!)
  • Dropper-ready
  • 2.6” tire clearance (2.4” with fenders)
  • Oversized Kickstand Plate
  • Eyelets for bolt-on frame bag
  • In-fork dynamo routing
  • Reynolds 853 Tubing
  • Custom UDH dropouts (singlespeedable, modular disc mount)

The preorder opens at noon today 10/23. Find all the details over at Klink Cycles.
